subject: Staggered micro-patch runbook & network drain plan for Private VPC estates
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, infra-team@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-05-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed staggered micro-patch cadence + network drain requirements

Team —

We ran the dry-run yesterday (attached) and surfaced a handful of timing and network considerations that should change how we schedule Private patches for customers on VPCs. High-level proposal:

- Move from large-wave patching to 5–10 node micro-waves (15–30m per wave) for latency-sensitive estates.
- Require a brief BGP/NAT drain step before each wave for customers that announce routes to their on-prem gateways.
- Keep a 60m validation window after each CU (canary update) before continuing; abort criteria are spelled out below.

Key asks:
1) Karthik — confirm the KV-cache warmup/eviction behavior under 10-node waves and whether we need an explicit cache pre-warm step.
2) Soojin — draft the ops checklist for the BGP/NAT drain and re-advertise flow; include exact CLI commands we want customers to run (or script).
3) Olga — update our rollback runbook to include a one-step unpin + soak on a standby fleet approach (we discussed last week).

Attachments: patch_manifest_v2.1.csv, preflight-checklist.md, dryrun-log-20260521.txt

Thanks — Steph
--
Stephanie Nguyen
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed staggered micro-patch cadence + network drain requirements

Stephanie — thanks for the notes and dry-run log. Short answers:

- KV-cache: 10-node micro-waves are fine for hot-prefix retention for typical seq lengths (<=1024). We saw a 6–8% cold-start token latency on the second wave in the dry run; that's the warmup edge-case you flagged.
- Pre-warm: I recommend a pre-warm step when we expect long-tail sessions: issue a small synthetic traffic burst (3m) to prime the cache after each wave completes. This can run from the standby fleet to avoid customer impact.

I've added a short checklist snippet to the drive link (INF-3421) with kernel-affinity knobs for the micro-wave executor. Will follow up with metrics thresholds for the canary window.

- Karthik
--

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-21T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed staggered micro-patch cadence + network drain requirements

Looping in Lara from AcmeCloud for confirmation on their side. Draft of the BGP/NAT drain steps (ops checklist):

1) Announce: set community tag NO_EXPORT on canary nodes.
2) Re-route: update route-maps to prefer standby gateways for new sessions (5m).
3) NAT drain: reduce conntrack timeout to 30s, wait 2x timeout, then remove node from pool.
4) Verify: run tcpdump sampling for 2m to confirm no new client SYNs.
5) Apply patch and health-check for 10m.
6) Re-advertise: restore original route-maps and conntrack settings, verify stateful translation counts.

CLI examples are in the attached preflight-checklist.md. If AcmeCloud is comfortable, we can include these as part of the SOW for private upgrades.

- Soojin

Date: 2026-05-21T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed staggered micro-patch cadence + network drain requirements

Soojin / team — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of notes from our side after a quick read of the dry-run:

- The NO_EXPORT step is doable but we prefer automation. We will add a playbook to set the community tag driven by your orchestration webhook.
- Conntrack ramp: our on-prem NAT boxes default to 120s timeouts; we will provide a short-lived config that switches to 30s for maintenance windows.
- Validation: we'll run a traffic mirror to the standby fleet for the 10m post-patch window and provide logs.

One ask from AcmeCloud: can Redwood provide a one-command rollback toggle that will both unpin and swap traffic back to the pre-update image? That will help our SOC team feel comfortable during the canary windows.

Regards,
Lara

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-22T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed staggered micro-patch cadence + network drain requirements

Thanks everyone — consolidated plan and next steps below. I took inputs from the dry run and Lara's asks and drafted a short emergency rollback toggle flow we can expose as a CLI and webhook. Summary: 

- Wave size: 5–8 nodes (customer-configurable) with 60m validation window.
- Pre-warm: synthetic priming burst (3m) from standby fleet immediately after each wave.
- Network drain: follow Soojin's 6-step checklist; AcmeCloud to provide automation hook for NO_EXPORT tagging.
- Rollback toggle: CLI target-unpin --env <env> --wave <id> which will: 
  - mark nodes for immediate traffic swap to standby image,
  - set model pins back to prior version in control-plane,
  - trigger KV-cache purge on updated nodes, and
  - create an incident stub (auto-attach logs).

Abort/rollback criteria (any one triggers rollback): 
- >5% token-latency regression sustained for 10m in canary metrics
- >0.5% increase in 5xx rates on canary instances
- Data path errors or conntrack breaches reported by customer

Action items (owners):
- Karthik: add pre-warm job to executor and expose a flag in the patch manifest (due 2026-05-25).
- Soojin: finalize CLI snippets and preflight playbook (due 2026-05-24).
- Marissa: update SOW language and runbook (due 2026-05-26).
- Steph: schedule coordination call with AcmeCloud and BankCorp ops for 2026-05-28 10:00 PT (invite pending).

Attachments referenced: patch_manifest_v2.1.csv, preflight-checklist.md (contains CLI examples), dryrun-log-20260521.txt

If no objections, I'll push the rollback toggle draft to the internal repo and create a test harness for the CLI toggle this week.

—Olga
